references.text: Jesus warns the disciples in the mission discourse that they will be hated by all for his name's sake – almost identical wording: "you will be hated by all for my name's sake" ([ref:Matt 10:22|Matthew 10:22]).

In the great eschatological discourse in Matthew, Jesus says that the disciples will be hated by all nations for his name's sake ([ref:Matt 24:9|Matthew 24:9]), a parallel to Luke's version of the same speech.
Mark's parallel to the eschatological discourse contains the same formulation: "you will be hated by all for my name's sake" ([ref:Mark 13:13|Mark 13:13]).

Jesus explains that the world hates the disciples because it first hated him, and that persecution occurs "for his name's sake" ([ref:Joh 15:18-21|John 15:18-21]). This elaborates on the reason for the hatred mentioned in Luke 21:17.
In the high priestly prayer, Jesus says that the world has hated the disciples because they are not of the world ([ref:Joh 17:14|John 17:14]), confirming the promise of hatred from the world.
John urges believers not to be surprised that the world hates them ([ref:1 Joh 3:13|1 John 3:13]), showing the fulfillment of Jesus' prophecy.

The apostles left the council rejoicing because they had been counted worthy to suffer disgrace for Jesus' name's sake ([ref:Apg 5:41|Acts 5:41]), an early fulfillment of Jesus' words about being hated for his name.

Isaiah prophesies that the faithful will be hated and cast out by their own brothers for the Lord's name's sake ([ref:Jes 66:5|Isaiah 66:5]), an Old Testament background for the theme of hatred toward God's people.
